text:
Maya: FYI customer hit a sustained 429s on embeddings during a nightly bulk job, asking for help. They say it started after switching to larger batches.
Maya: Details from customer: model=embed-large, batch_size=1024, concurrency=24 across 6 workers, payloads ~1.2k vectors per minute. Getting 429 with Retry-After 1-3s.
Maya: attaching their snippet of the request headers they logged:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Customer-Id: acme-inc
{ model: "embed-large", input: [...] }
```
Luca: Thanks — can you paste the exact 429 response headers they saw (x-rate-limit-*, retry-after)? that helps determine if this is burst window or sustained quota.
Maya: They sent this back: `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 1680000003`, `retry-after: 2` and body `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"burst limit exceeded"}`.
Priya: "burst limit exceeded" implies the per-tenant burst token bucket tripped (we have a short window to absorb spikes). Large batch + many concurrent workers will spike instantaneous token usage, even if long-run throughput is fine.
Carlos: Customer mentioned they recently increased batch_size from 256->1024 to save per-token cost. That matches.
Maya: They also observed occasional dimension mismatch errors from an older client (embedding dim=1024) but most 429s are separate. They upgraded client, 429s persisted.
Luca: I'm going to check SRE logs for the tenant window. Priya, any quick mitigation we can recommend before we look infra-side?
Priya: Recommend 3-prong: 1) reduce batch_size to 256-512, 2) add randomized exponential backoff with jitter on 429, 3) pace concurrency so total in-flight batches <= 8 for now. Send a sample backoff snippet we can give them.
Maya: I'll send a short repro script suggestion and the backoff snippet.
Maya: backoff snippet to customer:
```js
// simple exponential backoff with jitter
async function postWithBackoff(req, maxAttempts=6){
  for(let i=0;i<maxAttempts;i++){
    const res = await fetch('/v1/embeddings', req);
    if(res.status !== 429) return res;
    const wait = Math.min(1000 * 2**i, 20000); // cap 20s
    const jitter = Math.random()*200;
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, wait + jitter));
  }
  throw new Error('max retries reached');
}
```
Luca: Pulled logs for tenant `acme-inc` — saw repeated entries around thread_ts with reason `burst_window_exceeded` and our admission controller returning 429s. Log snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T02:12:31Z] tenant=acme-inc req_id=abc123 tokens_req=1024 window_tokens_left=0 reason=burst_window_exceeded
[2026-03-10T02:12:33Z] tenant=acme-inc req_id=abc124 tokens_req=1024 window_tokens_left=0 reason=burst_window_exceeded
```
Luca: Confirms burst bucket empties within the short window. This isn't the global hard quota, it's the short burst smoothing.
Priya: For long jobs we should also recommend the customer enable prefix/KV caching if they reuse inputs, and use smaller logical batches (combine fewer vectors per HTTP request) or use our streaming/incremental batching API.
Carlos: Customer asked if we can temporarily bump burst limits while they re-architect. Is that something we can safely do?
Luca: We can do a short-lived override for support but prefer to guide them to pacing. If they need it, we can create a 24-48h uplift for their tenant's burst window. Need approver.
Priya: Note: if they expect consistent sustained throughput at that scale we should steer them to Dedicated capacity — that guarantees the throughput without burst rejects.
Maya: I've drafted reply to customer with mitigation steps and the backoff snippet, plus offer for a temporary uplift + pointer to Dedicated. Asking for logs/ timestamps to match our traces.
Carlos: +1. Include suggested config: batch_size=256, parallel_workers=6, concurrency_limit_per_worker=2, retry policy as above. Also add probe step: run a 10m test with `ab` or simple loop and include `x-rate-limit-*` headers each request.
Maya: I'll send that now. tagging @Priya and @Luca for any edits.
Priya: lgtm. Also added note: if they still see 429s after pacing, include dump of request ids so SRE can do tail-sampling.
Maya: Customer accepted pacing steps and will run the 10m test tonight. I'll follow up after their run. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0310-embed-burst-acme-inc (assigned to SRE).
Carlos: Thanks team — good triage. We'll keep thread open until post-test follow-up. :white_check_mark:
